summary: Created dedicated system account `inventorysvc` on node1 and configured /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker to run as systemd service `inventory-worker` under that account, enabled and running. Completed mandatory single-node restart evidence: baseline boot_id captured, native reboot performed, boot_id change confirmed, and service/user recovery verified post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker (simple sleep-loop script with TERM/INT trap)
Created system user inventorysvc (no home, nologin shell) via useradd --system

Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User=inventorysvc, Group=inventorysvc, ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, Restart=on-failure, plus NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem/ProtectHome hardening
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, then enable --now on the service
Verified via ps and systemctl show that the running process was owned by inventorysvc and the service was active+enabled
Captured baseline boot_id and baseline service health
Triggered 'sudo shutdown -r now' backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again after reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed (513c865e... -> 786a8030...), proving a genuine restart
Re-verified post-reboot that inventory-worker.service auto-started (enabled), is active/running, and the new process still runs as inventorysvc

evidence.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as systemd service inventory-worker under dedicated inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: inventorysvc user created (no prior existence confirmed), unit file installed, service enabled+started, and ps/systemctl show confirm the process runs as inventorysvc, not root.
Captured baseline boot_id (513c865e-e121-4025-a0a4-8689cc580398) and confirmed inventory-worker.service was active and enabled before restart.
Issued 'sudo shutdown -r now' backgrounded; acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection failures during reboot, then a new boot_id (786a8030-a1ff-4d26-a7f9-f09ad108c932) different from baseline, proving the node actually restarted.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: recovered service/account state
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows inventory-worker.service active and enabled with a new MainPID (734), process still running under user/group inventorysvc.
